caption:
Padwa. He asked what she wanted. She said kahi nako, nothing at all. He believed her.

So she tied the knot herself: the Kiss Knot Bangle, a ribbed coil whose two ends cross under one polished X. 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated, ₹1,199.

We wear both, knots on top. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ kiss knot bangle · gold tone or rhodium · tied the knot, with herself ]
first_comment: Kahi nako, every single year. Tag her. Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #DiwaliPadwa #Padwa #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: Short video. An illustrated blush pink Art Deco building at night, four storeys with a pink paper lantern beside every window, six windows lit. The lantern beside a second-floor window lights up and the view moves in to it: a blush voile curtain drawn across the window, glowing from a lamp inside and stirring slightly. On the curtain the words appear in turn: 'Padwa. he asked what she wanted.', then the Marathi words kahi nako with the gloss 'kahi nako: nothing at all.' under them, then AND HE BELIEVED HER. The curtain draws aside to the right and is tied back, and the lamp lights the windowsill: a closed blush gift box with the Naira wordmark on its lid. Its drawer slides out onto dark velvet, where a bangle appears first as a drawn outline and then as the real photograph: a gold-tone ribbed coil bangle whose two ends cross under one polished X. A gleam runs along the coil to the X and a small sparkle catches on it, then the line 'so she tied the knot herself.' appears. A brass plate below the window reads FLAT 203. The view pulls back to the whole building with seven windows lit, then a closing card: Flat 203, second floor. Kiss Knot Bangle, 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated. ₹1,199. nairaflore.com. Two ends, one kiss. Wear both, knots on top. Every piece arrives in our blush box, free insured shipping, COD available.

On the windowsill a blush gift box with the Naira wordmark on its lid has its drawer pulled out on dark velvet, holding a gold-tone ribbed coil bangle whose two ends cross under a polished X. sound: In-app instrumental (Instagram audio library, no vocals, no lyrics): a light, wry piece with comic timing, piano with pizzicato strings, unhurried (search 'playful piano pizzicato calm'), entering at 0.6 s under the ambience, ducked 4 dB under the foley, and dipped -12 dB for 0.6 s at 6.5 s as AND HE BELIEVED HER. lands (the one-beat pause). BAKED into reel.mp4 (synthesised, _build/sfx.py, peak -12.5 dBFS in the mux): 0.0-1.2 s building ambience (street hum, a far scooter passing, a few evening birds; the bed stays on low and rises again over the last 0.6 s so the loop meets itself); 0.20 s the lift-bell, one soft brass ding (B5, ~1.2 s decay) as FLAT 203's kandil lights; 8.00-9.60 s the voile's rings on a brass rod, a soft metallic swish that follows the panel's own leading edge, with a small clink as each of nine rings meets the bunch; 9.80 s the drawer, a card-on-card slide following the REVEAL curve; 11.75 s one teaspoon ting on a steel tumbler with the sparkle on the X, 0.1 s before the turn rises; 16.55 s one low chime (E4-B4-E5) as the end card comes in (16.35 s until the 27 Oct pull-back fix moved the end card +0.2 s).
deviations: FIX 1, CURTAIN HAND-OFF, as asked with three refinements, all in world/bays/p07.js (builders2 untouched, P6 unaffected). (a) The panel's width now eases onto the drape: 60 + 720 (1 - m)^2 px from the jamb. The builder's straight lerp leaves it 98 px wide at m .94; this one is 62.6 px (x 867-930) there, the 'about 60 px' the fix asks for. (b) The cross runs over m .94-.97, not .94-1. At the cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) curve m .94-1 is 9.23-9.60 s, 11 frames. Over .94-.97 it is 9.23-9.32 s, the asked 'about 3 frames' (one mid-cross frame at 9.27 s). (c) The builder's drape is drawn pinched at the tie (37 px), so after the cross it hung cinched by nothing for 0.3 s. This bay now draws its own drape (the builder's drawing line for line, the waist a parameter): it hangs straight (59 px) at the hand-off, so the two outlines match top to bottom, and the waist is drawn in to 37 px as the tie-back fades in over 9.60-9.95 s, sliding 6 px toward the jamb. The builder's drape is hidden in this bay.

FIX 2a, BOX TEASE, CORRECTED (final review, 27 Oct): the last pass said no box ghosted through the drawn voile. It did. Its fade (box opacity over m .03-.15, contact shadows over .12-.24) left the box fully opaque behind the fabric from 8.54 s, and the panel's backdrop-filter blur(4px) is captured by Chromium and then scaled with the panel's scaleX about the jamb, so it drew the room misregistered and stretched: on the shipped mp4 a box about 1.5x wide, its lid print twice (about 250 px apart) and a grey chevron of its contact shadow inside the fabric, f253-f267 (8.43-8.90 s; the old reel against its own box-off render: 15 381-33 219 px a frame over 12 levels inside the panel at f255-f265, 0 by f273), and the same ghost in states.jpg's OPENING .50 tile. NOW, the director's fix as specified, in world/bays/p07.js: (a) setVoile sets the panels' backdropFilter to 'none' for every m > 0 and keeps blur(4px) only at m = 0; (b) the box's opacity ramp and the contact-shadow ramp are gone (box opacity 1, shadows at their full .34 / .38 from m 0), and apply() clips the box's own layer to the room left of the panel's live leading edge, leaning with the sway as the glow's clip does: sBox.style.clipPath = m < 1 ? polygon(0 0, (L + 6)px 0, (L + 6 + 960 tan a)px 960px, 0 960px) : 'none'. The box is never drawn behind the fabric; the 14 px hem uncovers it as it passes (first drawn at f258, m .208, 8.60 s: 245 px at 1 level under the hem's edge; seen from f259, 8.63 s). The cut lies 6 px in from the panel's edge, under the hem; the camera is at rest (e = 1) through the draw, so room and front px agree.

FINAL REVIEW FIX 1, WHAT ELSE IT MOVES (measured, kept): (i) the 4 px blur goes at 8.0 s (f241), the first frame of the draw: behind the fabric it was softening only the sill's back-edge band and arris, which now read sharp through it (a band of about 1.5 L*); the window's frame change f240 -> f241 is mean 0.24 L* against 0.21 for the next, motion-only step, and it shows only on a contrast stretch. (ii) when the clip lifts at m = 1 (f288, 9.60 s) the box re-rasterises by a dither: mean -0.14 levels, 785 px over 2 levels, at most 6 at a shadow edge (PNG, f280 against f288), below the encode's noise. (iii) the m = 1 stills are unchanged: cover.html renders byte-identical to the reviewed cover@2x.png (so cover.jpg, cover-grid.jpg, -45, -thumb and cover-thumb.png are the reviewed files, not re-exported); the reel's frames at 9.7, 12.5, 16.5, 16.9 and 18.0 s (the end card's fade and hold) render byte-identical with the old and the new bay, and so do 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 s at m = 0 (frame 0: 1 704 px at 1 level). (iv) the reel was re-rendered on the shared world as it stood at 01:04 UTC, so the bays other designers edited since the 23:23 render (P1, P2, P3, P4 and P12 at least) appear as they were then; p04.js (FLAT 103, below this window in the find and the pull-back) changed again at 01:11 and p11.js at 01:10, after this render began.

FIX 2b, GLOW: the transmitted radial is the brief's lamp (#FFE3CC 40 % peak, 900 x 700 at tile (300, 520), screen). A multiply falloff (#D9B3A9, 0 inside .38 of a 1960 x 1640 radial about the lamp, .22 at .75, .36 at the edge) deepens the far side. Measured on the frame at 6.0 s: lamp side L 96.0 (pass 1: 94.8), lower right L 85.8 (pass 1: 90.8, -5.5 %), so lamp to far corner is now 10.2 L (pass 1: 4.0).

FIX 2c, SWAY: skewX about the rod at the stated ±0.35 deg on a 5.0 s sine (reel T.sway / T.swayP). At the voile's 960 px drop that is ±5.9 px at the hem (measured 12.1 px peak to peak), not the '2-3 px' in the same line: the angle and the travel disagree, so I kept the angle. The type's band moves under ±2 px. Set T.sway = .17 for ±2.9 px. The leading hem strip, the catch-light and the glow and falloff clips lean with it. It passes zero at 8.0 s and fades out over the first 30 % of the draw (by 8.68 s). The panel runs 10 px past both jambs while it hangs across, so the lean never opens a sliver at either side.

FIX 2d, FOLDS: this bay draws its own panel art. Each fold's ridge (white .30) and valley (#A88A84, its own depth .18-.36) are trapezoids narrowing to 75 % at the rod about the fold's centre, under one horizontal blur (sigma 6), with the kit's heading pleats re-seated on the narrower tops. The CLOSED catch-light is now built from the same art ('catch' mode, ridges and pleats), not a clone of the panel.

FIX 3b, OUTLINE FADE: keyed on the develop as asked, but over dev .2-.9, not the stated .35-.75. The develop is the system's 0.9 s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), which reaches .35 at 10.58 s and .75 at 10.72 s, so (dev - .35) / .4 is a 0.13 s (4-frame) blink with the outline still 13 % undrawn. The stated 'overlaps the photograph by at least 0.4 s' holds only for a linear develop. Now: opacity .89 at dev .35, .61 at .5, .11 at .75, 0 at .9 (10.54-10.84 s, 9 frames), overlapping the photograph 10.50-10.84 s (0.34 s). For the outline to be complete before the photograph starts, it is drawn in 0.65 s (9.80-10.45 s, was 1.05 s). The retract starts at 10.55 s (fix 5 says 10.70 s) so its shape, the loop opening from the knot both ways, plays inside the fade. At 10.70 s the line is already at .12, and a later retract would never be seen.

FIX 3a: re-traced at sigma 4 native / approximate_polygon 3 (33 and 26 points), each a closed Catmull-Rom spline written as cubics (the system's C-OUTLINE asks sigma 1 / 1.5 / straight segments: that is what read as a zigzag at 2x). The knot's lobes are now soft bumps in the opening and under the coil, as in the photograph.
